Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the initial RFP packet — Ardent's procurement & security teams reviewed the materials overnight and have a couple of focused asks we hope you can clarify before we progress to the technical deep-dive: 

1) We need a concise mapping of Redwood controls and deliverables to the NIST AI RMF categories (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, Protect) — ideally a spreadsheet with control owner and evidence artifacts.
2) Please confirm how Redwood interprets "high-risk" under the EU AI Act for hosted inference. If you classify certain patterns as high-risk, we need the mitigations and documentation you would provide.
3) Evaluation & regression approach: procurement wants the proposed cadence, sampling strategy (how samples are chosen from production), and rollback-policy thresholds for model rollouts.

Can you confirm you can deliver the mapping (spreadsheet) and a one-page evaluation cadence summary by EOD Friday? Also let us know if you need an NDA amendment to share certain evidence artifacts.

Appreciate it — we are aiming to finalize the assurance annex by the second week of February.

Best,
Lenora

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 14:17:00 -0800
Subject: internal: draft mapping + sampling proposal

Team — early draft notes for the spreadsheet and the cadence doc. Key technical points to include so Ardent gets a clear, production-focused answer: 

- NIST mapping: map our controls to the 5 functions, and for each control list a representative artifact: e.g., 
  * Measure -> Model evaluation metrics & regression reports -> evidence: "evaluation-run-2025-12.pdf"; owner: Research QA.
  * Protect -> Encryption at rest & in transit -> evidence: KMS config exports; owner: Infra Security.

- EU AI Act position (short): Redwood treats hosted inference as a configurable service; classification as "high-risk" is workload-dependent. For generic text-generation we do not assert blanket high-risk status; for regulated decision-support (medical triage, loan adjudication) we recommend customers declare high-risk and we provide hardened deployment patterns (private deployments, detailed traceability, expanded logging/retention).

- Sampling & regression approach (technical):
  * Production sampling: we propose stratified sampling across traffic by route, tenant size, and prompt shape. Default: 0.5% of requests captured for daily micro-evals; configurable up to 2% for critical customers.
  * Regression runs: weekly automated smoke-run across seeded prompt sets + monthly full regression across expanded corpus (3k prompts stratified by intent and length).
  * Canary rollouts: progressive traffic shift (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated checks at each step: latency deviation >25% OR token-quality regression (BLEU/embedding drift/LLM-specific metric) beyond configured thresholds triggers automatic rollback.
  * Evidence artifacts: sample ids + anonymized transcripts stored in a walled-off evidence bucket for auditor access.

I'll attach a short notes file and a sample mapping spreadsheet. Priyom, please add any operational SLAs or compliance items I missed.

Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer
[Attachment: Regression_Sampling_Notes.md (markdown)]
[Attachment: Redwood_NIST_Mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Jan 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: internal: draft mapping + sampling proposal

Thanks Karthik — this is good. A couple of additions before we send to Ardent: 

1) EU AI Act: explicitly call out the artifacts we can provide for high-risk declarations: (a) model lineage & provenance export (model id, training snapshot, quantization profile); (b) evaluation sampling logs with hash-based anonymization; (c) traceability report mapping user input -> model variant -> output hash for a given invocation window.

2) Rollout thresholds: propose one additional metric for quality — "semantic drift" as measured by embedding cosine drift on a rolling baseline; threshold: >0.12 avg drift over evaluation window OR failure in accuracy for critical labeled prompts (pre-agreed set) -> HOLD. Add rollback contact list and SLAs for time-to-rollback (under 5 minutes for critical customers on dedicated pools).

3) Deliverables: update the spreadsheet with a column "EvidenceType" and a short appendix describing redaction/anonymization process for production sample sharing.

I attached our Assurance Appendix (boilerplate) and the evaluation cadence PDF for review. If we're comfortable with the EU language, I can produce the one-pager tonight.

— Priyom
Head of Evals & Assurance
[Attachment: Redwood_Assurance_Appendix.pdf (pdf)]

- We do not treat hosted inference as categorically "high-risk"; classification depends on customer workload. For customers with regulated decision-support, Redwood supports hardened deployments and expanded evidence deliverables (lineage, traceability exports, extended logs).
- Sampling: default 0.5% stratified capture; configurable to 2% for tighter audit needs. Regression cadence: weekly smoke + monthly full regression across ~3k stratified prompts.
- Rollouts: progressive canary with automated checks (latency, token-quality metrics, embedding drift). Configured thresholds will be agreed in the annex; critical customers can opt into faster rollback SLAs on dedicated pools.
